title: The September cut took 17% of my Claude Code week. Subagents were taking 48%.
why_read: A detailed, data-driven dissection of how AI coding agent subagents consume disproportionate usage quota, useful for heavy Claude Code users optimizing cost and workflow.
analysis: The author analyzed their own actual usage logs, 455 sessions and 63,000 requests, to figure out why their weekly AI coding quota was running out faster after a service change. They found that subagents, helper processes spawned to do subtasks, were consuming a much larger share of tokens than the user's own direct interactions. They also caught and corrected a double-counting bug in the raw logs that would have overstated token usage by roughly double. This is a concrete, reproducible-methodology piece of real operational data about a widely used AI coding tool, which is genuinely useful for other heavy users trying to manage cost and quota.
